chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you are an Imam (leading prayer), recite Surah Al-Fatiha in the last two rak'ahs; and if you are praying alone, it is permissible for you whether you do or do not."

key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: Is reciting Surah Al-Fatiha obligatory in the last two rak'ahs for the Imam and the individual?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between the Imam's obligation to recite Surah Al-Fatiha in the final two rak'ahs of congregational prayer and the permissibility of silence or recitation for the individual worshiper. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that while the Imam's recitation is mandatory for the congregation's validity, the individual has flexibility, highlighting the structural hierarchy in communal worship. This ruling underscores the importance of the Imam's role in leading the prayer while acknowledging the autonomy of personal devotion.
